html:
The Wattasids were a Berber dynasty that ruled northern Morocco from Fez, from 1472 to 1554. They are shown here in 1492 and 1500. The map calls their state a caliphate; they ruled as sultans.

They were a branch of the same Zenata tribes as the Marinids and served as their viziers, the real power behind weak sultans. After a revolt in Fez overthrew the last Marinid in 1465, the Wattasid Muhammad al-Shaykh took the city in 1472 and made himself sultan.

Their reach was small. Portugal held Ceuta and took Asilah and Tangier in 1471, and kept seizing ports on the Atlantic coast. In 1492 refugees from the fall of Granada arrived in Fez; among them was the boy who became Leo Africanus. In the south, the Saadi dynasty rose by leading holy war against the Portuguese. The later Wattasid years are on the page Watassid Morocco.
